pages.text: "Not yet! The cousins have not gone in!" Lulu lined olive pits across the attic floor. The wooden shutters stood wide open. The yard grew dark.
Mom came upstairs. "Lulu, time to close the shutters." "Not sleepy at all!" Lulu shook the head and swept the pits together.
But the eyelids kept drooping. A pit fell from a blunt hand, and a yawn escaped. "Why are my eyelids so heavy?"
Mom held Lulu at the window. The whole farmhouse yard lay below. "Look there." She pointed to the downstairs windows.
Clack! A shutter closed at the cousins' room. Clack at the next window, then the next. The yard became dark and quiet.
"See? Shutters closed means everyone sleeps," Mom whispered. Only Lulu's window remained open. "Shutters closed, time for sleep!"
Lulu held the shutter with a blunt hand and shut it. The blue bell jingled. "All our house's windows have closed their eyes!"
Lulu slipped under the blanket. Mom kissed the forehead and blew out the lamp. Thin starlight came through the shutter cracks.
Mom unfolded her fingers. "One, stop playing when shutters close! Two, under the blanket! Three, lamp out and sleep!" Lulu's long ears fell on the blanket. Both eyes slowly closed.
Mom hugged Lulu and tucked the blanket to the chin. With shutters closed, the blanket felt so soft. "Sleep well, Lulu. Shutters closed, time for sleep!"
